comment: The Prism as a whole, after /mnt/project-files/prism-purpose/what-my-prism-is.md: its OPM system diagram (ISO 19450) at the top of its architecture description (ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010). The LexLean generator generators/GenSystem.lex.tex writes app/src/PrismSystem.lex.tex from it (tools/generators/run.sh); SY-01 and GN-01 hold the two equal. Every decision of app/prompts/set.json is one part's; a part no decision realizes says what it owes, and the owed parts only shrink (GenSystem::mayOwe). Each standard is named by its key in the standards register.
name: Prism
text: The whole Prism: a digital twin of one person that is also their personal agent, run only in that person's own browser; one model, proved in Lean, compiled into one content-addressed holo.
frame: a digital twin of one person that is also their personal agent, differentiating and routing what reaches them

beneficiary.name: Person
beneficiary.text: The one person the Prism is a digital twin of: its stakeholder, its beneficiary and its only agent, who acts by their own gestures and is a part of the Prism (ISO/IEC 30173 physical counterpart; IEEE P7006 the agent's person).

counterpart: The person, the twin's physical counterpart, outside the browser and also a part of the Prism.

attribute.name: Hold on their own information
attribute.text: Whether what reaches the person is understood, with nothing slipping: the attribute of the person the Prism's main process changes.

input.name: Person's streams
input.text: The services where the person's life arrives: mail and calendar first, device files, then the person's other services, read only as the person's own browser shows them.

result.name: Held content
result.text: Content-addressed objects held only in the person's browser, from which the person's view and outgoing acts are made.

parts.name: Me
parts.owed: The declared identity is a product requirement (requires.identity in app/specs/product) that no decision yet decides.

parts.name: Synchronisation
parts.owed: ISO/IEC 30188 asks a twin to keep its state in step with its counterpart; no decision yet holds the twin's state of the person, or how it is kept current from the streams and the person's gestures and corrected by the person.

standards: ISO/IEC 30173:2023 Digital twin, concepts and terminology
The Prism is a digital twin and the person its physical counterpart; the twin's terms are the standard's.
The twin's reference architecture, and the synchronisation between twin and person (the Synchronisation part).
IEEE P7006 Personal Data Artificial Intelligence Agent
The Prism is the person's agent: it serves only its person, acts within their terms and is accountable to them.
Each held item's quality: currentness, accuracy, completeness, consistency, credibility and understandability.
Relevance judged against the person's tasks and context, conformity with their expectations, controllability and engagement.
ISO 9241-112:2017 Principles for the presentation of information
What is shown is detectable, free of distraction, discriminable, interpretable, concise and consistent.
The person's goals, tasks and context of use, against which each part's usability is measured.
The system's stakeholder, concern, viewpoint and view, at the top of the architecture description.
The system diagram: main process, beneficiary and its attribute's states, agent, instruments, inputs, results, and its zoom into the parts.
